title: Reconstruction of a supplied adic-lisse model
statement: Let X and Y be schemes, i:Y→X an immersion and U an object of Y_proet. Let A be a commutative coefficient ring with an adic coefficient datum d [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let K be intrinsically complete over the completed coefficient sheaf on X [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For any integers a,b and any supplied common local model L of the canonical reduction tower of K on g=U.hom≫i [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], the complex Q(L.complex) is isomorphic to g^*K as a complex of modules over the actual inverse-image completed coefficient ring.

source.place: Proof steps 9--10: completeness and reconstruction of every supplied common local model.

proof.text: For the composite g of an immersion and a pro-etale covering object, use the over-site description of weakly etale inverse image and immersion preservation of small limits. The underlying additive-sheaf comparison and reflection of limits by forgetting module structure show that module inverse image preserves countable products. Products are exact on the pro-etale site. Localization of termwise products through Q therefore shows that the induced exact functor on derived categories preserves countable products. An additive triangulated functor preserving these products sends a Roos triangle to the Roos triangle for the image sequence: check the equation for 1-T after every product projection.

source.place: Proof steps 9--10: completeness and reconstruction of every supplied common local model. Argument part 1.

proof.text: Every relatively adic-lisse term is locally the inverse limit of the constant finite quotient modules in its local model. At each finite level an element a of the ideal acts nilpotently, so 1-aT on a countable product has inverse the finite geometric series. The inverses are compatible with the quotient maps. Limits and descent along the supplied covering sieve give invertibility on the term. Invertibility passes termwise to complexes and through constant-scalar restriction. In the Cech presentation of completed coefficients, the local completeness criterion for the ideal generated by a finite generating family, and the Koszul completion reflector, show intrinsic completeness of the model. The unit-compatible comparison between Koszul and quotient completion gives invertibility of its actual quotient-completion unit.

source.place: Proof steps 9--10: completeness and reconstruction of every supplied common local model. Argument part 2.

proof.text: Resolve the model by a K-flat complex with flat terms. The coefficient comparison g^{-1}A_X^hat = A_Y^hat and its finite-quotient comparisons identify the ordinary quotient monads. Their comparison respects the extension/restriction adjunction units. Because a quotient unit is epic, this unit equation implies compatibility with every quotient transition. The K-flat extension counits identify ordinary reductions with derived reductions; the derived composition comparison and its representative equation transport the ordinary compatibility to the derived sequences. Transport the canonical quotient-completion Roos triangle through the coefficient equivalence and then through the quasi-isomorphism of the resolution. It exhibits Q(L) as a derived inverse limit of the model reduction sequence.

source.place: Proof steps 9--10: completeness and reconstruction of every supplied common local model. Argument part 3.

proof.text: Intrinsic completeness of K makes its canonical quotient-completion unit an isomorphism by the Koszul/quotient comparison and independence of the representative. Its completion Roos triangle thus has vertex K. Apply the product-preserving derived inverse image from the first step to get a Roos triangle with vertex g^*K and sequence g^*(K_n).

source.place: Proof steps 9--10: completeness and reconstruction of every supplied common local model. Argument part 4.

proof.text: The supplied model identifications, its compatibility with normalizations, and the evaluation law of the canonical reduction tower identify the two sequences as completed-coefficient sequences, including consecutive transition maps. On products the levelwise isomorphisms conjugate 1-T. Transporting one distinguished triangle by the product isomorphism therefore gives a derived inverse limit for the other sequence. Uniqueness up to isomorphism of derived inverse limits gives Q(L) isomorphic to g^*K. This uses neither a choice of a strict-tower lift nor uniqueness of such a lift.

lean.statement:
theorem pbc_suppliedModel_reconstruction
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (U : Y.ProEt)
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (K : PbcCompletedDerived X d) (hK : PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete X d K)
    (a b : ℤ)
    (L : AdicTowerLocalModel d (U.hom ≫ i) (pbcReductionAdicTower X d K) a b) :
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L.complex ≅
      (adicTowerPullback (U.hom ≫ i) (pbcAdicCompletion X d)).obj K)
